scenario: Landing page must follow the 8-section story arc
description: Every Simply Enak landing page should follow: Hero → Problem → Tours → HowItWorks → Testimonials/Social Proof → FAQ → Final CTA. Tours must appear early, not buried after generic sections.
notes: Maarten: 'I don't really see a story arch or even a visual arch. I don't feel it's helping me buy a tour.' Tours shown FIRST, not buried.

scenario: Hero fields must not be null in Payload
description: Common bug: hero_title and hero_description are null in Payload DB even when content appears populated. Check all 3 tiers: live API → JSON snapshots → hardcoded data.
notes: Root cause: _status filter in getLandingPages() rejects draft entries.

scenario: All content must have complete MS locale coverage
description: Every route, tour, landing page, blog post, story must have a complete MS counterpart. No EN-only pages. Meta titles and descriptions also translated. BM pages must mirror EN structure section-for-section.
notes: Consolidated from lp_bm_mirrors_en + tour_bm_translated. 32 LP routes deployed en+ms.

scenario: Every tour must have all required fields populated in Payload
description: Check all bookable tours for complete data: description, itinerary, included/excluded, dietary options, images, pricing tiers, meeting point, max pax, what-to-bring, cancellation policy, languages, accessibility info.
notes: 4 core tours: Eat Drink George Town, Penang Street Food, KL Street Food, Flavours of Malaysia.

scenario: Known tour bugs must not regress
description: Regression tests for bugs found and fixed in prior sessions. Each test targets a specific root cause that has caused issues before.

regression_tests.description: Walking label must be 'Moderate Walking' not bare 'Moderate'
wheelchair accessibility field must exist and not be null
Bring Your Own vs Provided vs Not Allowed must be stated
Age requirement (All Ages / Adults 21+ / etc) must be present
Itinerary must be valid JSON array, not plain text

notes: From prior audit: 3 fields missing (wheelchair, alcohol, age), 5 tours had status:draft, walking label was 'Moderate' instead of 'Moderate Walking'.

scenario: Every page must pass SEO fundamentals
description: Title tags, meta descriptions, headings, canonicals, structured data, internal links. Check across all content types: tours, landing pages, blog posts, stories.
notes: Applies to all: tours, landing pages (32+), blog posts, stories.

scenario: Pages must have complete structured data markup
description: JSON-LD schema must be present and valid per content type: BlogPosting/BreadcrumbList for blogs, Product for tours, FAQPage for FAQ sections, LocalBusiness for homepage. Schema must validate against Google structured data rules.
notes: Consolidated from blog_schema_markup. Extended to all content types.

scenario: Content must match Simply Enak brand voice across all types
description: The Passionate Friend archetype across all copy: tour descriptions, landing pages, blog posts, emails. Success filter: WELCOMED, FASCINATED, CONNECTED. Content pillars: Tailored Experiences, Malaysia's Beauty, Sustainable Impact.
notes: Consolidated from blog_brand_voice. Extended to all content types. Banned words list and brand voice reference in Brilliant KB.

scenario: Image pipeline must produce optimized, accessible images
description: Every image needs: WebP format (or responsive), srcset for responsive loading, lazy loading below the fold, alt text, unique filenames, reasonable file size. Sharp WebP generation must work for all uploads.
notes: CF Free plan = no Polish/Image Resizing. Sharp WebP + Payload sizes required.

scenario: Every page must have correct Open Graph and Twitter Card tags
description: OG tags enable rich link previews on social media and messaging apps. Required: og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, og:type. Twitter Card: summary_large_image.
notes: Critical for social sharing of tours and blog posts.

scenario: System must pass pre-deploy readiness checks
description: Before any deploy: Payload API reachable, all env vars configured in Dokploy, no draft-only content published, build succeeds (720+ pages), OpenViking and Brilliant health endpoints respond.
notes: CI gate. If any hard requirement fails, block deploy.

scenario: Agent memory providers must be operational
description: Both OpenViking and Brilliant KB must be healthy and reachable. Basics: Hermes memory.provider set, endpoints respond, embeddings work, no circuit-breaker events.
notes: OpenViking at openviking.system.simplyenak.com. Brilliant MCP at brilliant-mcp.system.simplyenak.com.

scenario: Known infrastructure bugs must not regress
description: Regression tests for infrastructure bugs fixed in prior sessions. Each test targets a specific root cause.

regression_tests.description: Landing page query must not reject draft entries
New Payload collections must add payload_locked_documents_rels
No GraphQL type collisions across content types
Watchtower is monitor-only — deploys go through GH Actions
Versions/drafts disabled on pages with known field collisions
Hero fields must not be null even when content is draft status

notes: All fixed in prior sessions. Check for regressions on every deploy.

scenario: Accessibility fundamentals must be met
description: All images must have alt text. Heading hierarchy must be sequential (H1→H2→H3, no skips). Form inputs must have associated labels. Focus order must match visual order. No empty links or buttons.
notes: Static checks only. Full a11y audit requires screen reader testing.

scenario: Booking and contact flows must work end-to-end
description: HTTP integration test: tour page → CTA → enquiry form → submission → confirmation. Contact form must submit without 500 error. Email notifications trigger. Requires live server — not static file check.
notes: Critical path: tour page → enquiry → booking. Requires HTTP test harness — runner skips this case in static mode and reports 'needs integration test run'.

scenario: Pages must meet performance budgets
description: Astro builds must complete under 5 min. FCP < 2.5s. LCP < 4s. Page weight < 1.5MB. CLS < 0.1. These metrics require PageSpeed Insights API or Lighthouse CI — cannot be determined from static file checks alone.
notes: Requires PageSpeed Insights API key + CI integration. Runner skips in static mode. Build-time checks (duration, JS errors) can run locally.

scenario: All expected landing pages must exist and build
description: 32 LP segments across EN+MS = 64 pages. Plus segment landing pages. Every route from the LP plan must produce a static page at build time.
notes: MS locale routes for all 32 segment landing pages added recently.

scenario: Staging and production content must be in sync
description: Staging should reflect production content. Checks tour count, page count, media files across both environments. Requires access to both CF Pages deployments.
notes: CF Pages staging at separate URL. Runner skips if only one environment accessible.

scenario: Stories collection must be Discover-ready — scroll-stopping titles, featured images, no banned words, unique angle
description: Google Discover traffic requires different optimization than SEO: emotion-driven titles (70-95 chars), human-face/scroll-stopping images, no AI-sounding banned words, and information gain (unique first-person angle, not generic listicle). This check is warn-only — reports gaps but never blocks deploy.

expected_title_length.note: Discover sweet spot per publisher research

notes: Added Jul 2026. Discover optimization per Charles Float / Guim Shavein research. Stories are the primary editorial collection for algorithmic traffic. Warn-only because Discover-readiness is progressive content polish, not a deploy-blocking issue.

scenario: Every blog post must have an AI-optimized 2-3 sentence summary at the top
description: A concise answer-summary in the first visible paragraph improves AI overview extraction (Google SGE, ChatGPT citations). The summary should answer the core question in 2-4 sentences before any introductory prose. Pattern: bold 'TL;DR' lead-in, blockquote, or a question-answering first paragraph.
notes: From SEO video research, Jul 2026: 2-sentence summary at top led to #1 ranking + ChatGPT citation in <8 hours.

scenario: Blog posts must meet minimum word count for SEO depth
description: Content depth correlates with ranking position. Minimum 1,200 words for non-competitive terms ensures comprehensive answer. Posts under 1,000 words rarely rank for competitive food/travel keywords.
notes: From SEO video research, Jul 2026: 5,600-word post outranked 1,400-word competitor in under 8 hours.

scenario: The benchmark file itself must be valid
description: Meta-validation of the eval benchmark: all case_ids unique, JSON schema valid, weights between 0 and 1, all required fields present, no duplicate descriptions, no orphaned references.
notes: Run this first. If meta-integrity fails, other results are unreliable.

scenario: Blog posts must address the searcher immediately in the first paragraph (Caleb Ulku, Jul 2026)
description: From Caleb Ulku SEO podcast (Jul 2026): The first paragraph is the #1 missed opportunity. No 'history lesson' intros about founding year. Must contain target keyword in first 40 words. Must address what the searcher actually wants. Must include specific details (names, numbers, places).
notes: Caleb: title tag > H1 > first paragraph. Nobody searches 'plumber Houston' to read history lessons. Same applies to food tour content.

scenario: Blog posts must include specific attributes for AI agent recommendations (Caleb Ulku, Jul 2026)
description: From Caleb Ulku SEO podcast (Jul 2026): AI agents use attribute matching to recommend businesses. 'Halal food tour' — if you don't say 'halal-certified', you might not get recommended. Each post should include: specific dish names, location details, sensory descriptors, and dietary specificity. Google mass-deindexed AI slop that lacked real attributes.
notes: Caleb: Study the language that ranking pages use and mirror it. Make a list of required attributes for each piece. AI agents read your ENTIRE page and extract the most important parts.

scenario: Blog posts and stories must not show clusters of AI writing patterns
description: Detect clusters of AI-generated writing patterns based on ai-copywriter skill (v1.5.1) + blader/humanizer v2.9.1 + Wikipedia Signs of AI Writing guide. Each pattern alone is noise; 3+ different pattern groups in one piece is a signal. Checks: AI vocabulary (#7), signposting (#28), vague attributions (#5), filler phrases (#23), persuasive authority (#27), generic conclusions (#25), negative parallelisms (#9), copula avoidance (#8), rule of three overuse (#10), curly quotes (#19). Warn-only because pattern detection has false-positive risk — human review required before concluding.
notes: From mikiarlo3/ai-copywriter repo (MIT, 984 stars, updated Jul 2026). Detection only, never auto-rewrite. Warn-only because isolated tells are normal; clusters need human confirmation. Aligns with content-quality skill principle: detect, don't auto-polish.

scenario: Every location page must mention places findable on Google Maps
description: A location landing page that names no real place (street, neighbourhood, market, station, landmark, hotel, airport) is generic SEO filler. Users cannot orient themselves and AI agents cannot anchor the page to a real location. Every location page should reference at least one place a visitor could find on Google Maps.
notes: Maarten rule 2026-08-05: every location page should mention some places/locations that can be found on Google Maps.
